items.title: Louis Hayes interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: But with Cannon it wasn’t like that. Cannon was more spontaneous. We rehearsed, we had it together... I always enjoy, especially when you’re playing with creative people like Cannon

ctx.x: Did the band rehearse at all?

Yes, we rehearsed, but it wasn’t like Horace though. Now Horace rehearsed quite a bit. And when he went into the studio Horace — we had played the choruses, played the compositions, so all the little things were worked out, what we were going to do. But with Cannon it wasn’t like that. Cannon was more spontaneous. We rehearsed, we had it together, but everybody was so talented we didn’t — it was more spontaneous. We didn’t rehearse all the time like that.

Did you have a feeling when you did some of the tunes like “The Work Song” and “Jive Samba,” that these were going to be hits? I’m not sure how you define a hit in the jazz world. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-
